query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: number_of_distinct_problems
per_column.rationale: Count of problems addressed is extractable from the note and plausibly drives longer visits; it is a distinct variable from duration, not a restatement or component of it.

per_column.name: primary_problem_category
per_column.rationale: The clinical nature of the primary problem (trauma, procedural, chronic, etc.) is a legitimate covariate that carries signal about how long a visit takes, independent of the duration itself.

per_column.name: new_treatment_initiated
per_column.rationale: Whether a new treatment was started reflects visit content and plausibly correlates with duration; it is not deterministically the duration nor a mere restatement of it.

per_column.name: in_visit_procedure_or_intervention
per_column.rationale: The type of procedure performed during the visit is a substantive activity variable that strongly and plausibly predicts duration without being a component or deterministic function of it.

per_column.name: critical_or_life_threatening_status
per_column.rationale: Acuity/severity is a legitimate predictor of visit length, distinct from the duration measure; it carries signal but is not a restatement or leakage.

per_column.name: imaging_or_lab_testing_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of testing ordered is a workflow-content variable that plausibly extends visits and is distinct from the focus; a valid predictor.

per_column.name: specialist_referral_or_consultation
per_column.rationale: Whether a referral/consult occurred is a distinct visit-content variable plausibly associated with longer visits; not a component or restatement of duration.

judge.rationale: All seven columns are semantically distinct visit-content variables extractable from the note, each lying outside the focus (visit_duration_min) and none restating, componentially decomposing, or leaking it. Collectively they capture problem complexity, acuity, procedures, testing scope, treatment initiation, and referrals -- a coherent and largely non-redundant set of plausible drivers of visit length that add substantial predictive leverage beyond the original columns (department, urgency, age_group, reason). Some overlap exists (e.g., procedure vs. testing scope vs. treatment), slightly reducing marginal information, hence 0.8 rather than higher.
